title: Tenant throttle runbook and burst credit reconciliation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Post-incident follow-up for the capacity outage on 2026-02-26 where a bursty tenant caused eviction cascades across a Dedicated cluster. This ticket creates an operational runbook for quickly quieting noisy clients, a reconciliation procedure for burst credit accounting, and a set of engineering changes to prevent large reservation deficits that lead to mass evictions. Goal: reduce recurrence risk and provide a clear playbook for on-call to remediate in <30 minutes.
root_cause_summary: A high-throughput tenant with irregular spiky traffic exhausted transient reservation headroom and depleted its burst credit balance. The allocator's soft-burst path allowed sustained bursts longer than intended because token refill settings and credit decay windows were misaligned with observed sequence-length distributions. Simultaneously a KV-cache warmup spike increased memory and kernel pressure causing allocator-driven evictions. The combination produced a noisy-neighbor eviction storm that cascaded to adjacent tenants.
timeline_summary: 2026-02-26 03:12 UTC: first latency alerts. 03:18 UTC: evictions begin; autoscaler attempted to recover but allocation loop thrashed. 03:45 UTC: mitigation by emergency soft-quarantine for top offender (manual). 04:05 UTC: traffic throttled and cluster stabilized. Continuous tracing and metrics captured; incident declared Sev2 and postmortem opened.
mitigations_done: Manual soft-quarantine applied to offender tenant for 1h (reduced burst allowances)
Temporary increase of reservation guardrail for adjacent tenants to prevent immediate cascading evictions
Collection of full KV-cache heatmap and tenant-level burst credit traces for forensic analysis

acceptance_criteria: Runbook created and reviewed with SRE/serving-runtime/observability
Automated tenant quieting can be triggered by alert and reduces offender burst capacity without requiring manual intervention
Burst-credit reconciliation job runs daily and surfaces any tenant with negative or inconsistent balances to a triage dashboard
New burst token settings validated by synthetic spike tests and do not increase 95th percentile latency for non-offender tenants by >5%
Reservation audit CLI is available in ops toolkit and produces a per-tenant CSV report
rollout_plan: 1) Merge allocator and agent changes behind feature flag
2) Deploy to staging, run full synthetic and KV-cache warmup scenarios
3) Canary to one dedicated pool (low-traffic) for 48h while monitoring eviction/memory signals
4) If canary stable, ramp to 20% of pools, then to 100% in 24–48h increments
5) If anomalies observed, rollback new burst params and engage pause-and-investigate checklist
test_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket refill and decay logic
Integration tests for quieting flow including audit log emission and tenant state transitions
Synthetic workload generator for sustained spikes at multiple sequence-lengths to validate reservation hysteresis
Chaos test that simulates KV-cache cold-start under heavy burst to ensure no eviction cascade in canary
